r6_status.J-3: OPEN: versions.lock refuses an in-place edit only while the old registry entry remains; the design does not require validate-kit to detect rewriting that entry to the new object id, so a committed case/config edit plus registry rewrite can pass.

findings.claim: The version registry does not yet enforce its claimed append-only property. Validation compares current objects with current registry values, but a commit can edit an existing case/configuration and rewrite its registry entry to match, preserving the same semantic version and instrument tag.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:139-145 declares entries never rewritten but specifies only current-object equality; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:302-307 requires an in-place-edit refusal fixture without requiring a registry-rewrite fixture or a historical append-only check.
findings.fix: Require validate-kit to compare versions.lock with an authoritative historical baseline and reject deletion or alteration of existing mappings, permitting only new unique mappings. Add a fixture that commits an in-place object edit together with a rewritten lock entry and proves both validation and provisioning refuse it.

findings.claim: The documentation still does not fully pass the another-machine test for pinned runs: git cat-file recipes cannot recover an unreachable caseTree/configTree, and no procedure explains how to fetch the recorded measuring commit or otherwise obtain those objects before retrying.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:76-79 makes unreachable pins unreadable/refused; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:276-289 promises cross-machine resume and exact-byte recipes but names only git cat-file, not object acquisition or the unreachable-object recovery workflow.
findings.fix: Add a README procedure that uses measuringMetasystemSha to fetch the relevant commit/object graph from the documented repository remote, verifies caseTree/configTree availability, retries the operation, and states the terminal refusal when the objects cannot be obtained.

summary: The projection and compatibility tables now cover the shipped manifest fields and preserve all six aliases modulo the explicit equivalence differences; legacy resume, extractor identity, comparison ancestry, mission naming, bounded tags, raw-byte instrument integrity, and mandatory CLI version pins are coherent. J-1 and J-2 are closed. The remaining material gap is that versions.lock is called append-only without an enforceable historical check, so J-3 is not actually closed; the cross-machine documentation also omits recovery of unreachable pinned Git objects. No additional case/config abstraction or content-derived tag is needed.
